A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same boosting-inspired LLM training work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original Gemma 2 2B experiments on GSM8K and MBPP in Section 8, Tables 1–2, and the experimental appendices.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark experiments in Section 7, three-seed results in Table 1, and additional labeler and training-duration experiments in Appendix F.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 revises its generation/filtering stage to generate k responses and apply a noisy filter with recall parameter γ, replacing best-of-k selection and exact filtering. The weighted training loop remains. Keeping multiple correct responses was already used experimentally in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GSM8K mathematical reasoning and MBPP Python programming. The added labeler models and longer runs vary configurations and budgets within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark comparisons retain PT, Gold SFT, Do nothing, Filter only, and Boosting without focusing. Appendix F varies the labeler within Boosting rather than introducing an external comparison algorithm.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds experiments holding the Gemma 2 2B learner fixed while using Gemma 1 2B or Gemma 7B labelers, and extends selected GSM8K runs to ten rounds. Existing benchmark sample counts, per-round training budgets, prompting, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds substantive sensitivity and convergence diagnostics: stronger/weaker off-policy labelers and ten-round training to examine performance plateaus. Existing focusing ablations, weak-data variants, labeler-accuracy curves, response-length analyses, and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: V1 presents point estimates without seed counts or dispersion. V2 Table 1 and Figures 1–2 explicitly report means and sample standard deviations across three seeds. This substantially changes uncertainty reporting; v1 does not establish a previous run count.

E6.justification: The main results are replaced by three-seed estimates: GSM8K Boosting (A) test accuracy changes from .446 to .456, and Filter only from .371 to .393. MBPP Boosting (A) and Filter only now both report .329, versus .328 and .320. These are revised estimates, not demonstrated method gains between versions. Appendix F additionally reports labeler-strength effects and limited test improvement despite continued training improvement.

T1.justification: V2 introduces one-sided noisy filtering and changes the main theorem's sampling requirement from (2 log T + log |P|)/β to division by βγ. Appendix A revises the probability argument and adds an at-most-one-correct-response simplifying assumption. However, its assumed partition of prompts is not reconciled with Definition 2's per-response filtering rule.

C1.justification: The claimed convergence guarantee now encompasses imperfect filter recall, whereas v1's conclusion leaves imperfect filters to future work. The central claims about convergence from weak data, the boosting connection, and benefits of focused labeling remain.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds an empirical argument favoring recursive synthetic training over direct Gold SFT. Appendix F connects weaker-labeler performance to the expectation of needing more iterations and documents practical plateau behavior. Existing strong-learner limitations remain after relocation.

D1.justification: V2 newly discloses the Gemma Terms of Use and MIT licensing for GSM8K and MBPP in Section 7. Existing training details and Appendix D prompt templates are retained; this is additional licensing information, not evidence of changed resource availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds nine cited works and targeted discussion of noisy synthetic data, self-improvement theory, RLHF, and computational allocation, including Firdoussi, Song, and Yang. The central positioning around strong learners and continuous improvement remains.

P1.justification: The discussion is substantially reorganized: the boosting interpretation becomes Section 6.1, while weighting and nonsynthetic-data filtering discussions move to Appendix E. Appendix B/C content is redistributed, the abstract is shortened, and prose and reference ordering are edited.

P2.justification: V1 Tables 1–2 are merged into v2 Table 1 with uncertainty annotations. Existing benchmark plots gain error bars, the MBPP plot moves into the main text, Figures 5–6 are added, and qualitative-example tables are compacted and relocated.

improvement.justification: Three-seed uncertainty reporting and added labeler and ten-round diagnostics strengthen the empirical evidence. However, v2 Definition 2 allows a prompt into the rejected set even when another response is accepted, while Appendix A.1 and Lemma 10 require disjoint prompt sets and rejection only when no response is accepted. V1's best-of-k selection avoided this conflict. This unresolved mismatch affects the central theoretical extension, preventing a reliable net quality judgment despite the empirical benefits.
